sentences.text: As per the informant, his daughter (victim) aged 15 years was going on a bicycle to the agricultural field to provide meals to the informant and his son, when she was allegedly intercepted by the accused, who attempted to outrage her modesty.

A report was lodged initially under sections 354A,

sentences.text: , the victim made an improvement in her earlier testimony and also alleged commissioning of rape upon her.
It is for the first time in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. that such a version has surfaced.
The investigation concluded with submission of charge-sheet against the accused under sections 354A, 323, 506 I.P.C. read with section 8 of POCSO Act.
The victim was medically examined nearly two months after the incident and in such examination no internal injuries were found.
Certain superficial external injuries were noticed, which has been proved by doctor, PW-7.
The injuries included complain of pain in the right shoulder, swelling in the abdomen over an area of 4 X 2 cm. and complain of pain in the left leg.
The incident itself is of 3rd May, 2014.

The prosecutrix has supported the prosecution case with regard to the commissioning of offence of rape but the same has been disbelieved by the trial court after noticing that there was a material improvement in her version from what was disclosed earlier by her while recording her statement under section 161 Cr.P.C.

The court below has noticed that though the incident is of 3rd May, 2014 but it is only on 15th July, 2014 when the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded that the allegation with regard to commissioning of rape was made for the first time.
No reasons for such delayed disclosure of a serious offence has been put forth by the prosecution.
The father of the victim who has appeared as PW-1 has not supported the prosecution case and has turned hostile.
There are no other eye witnesses and the alleged complaint of the victim does not find any corroboration from the medical evidence on record.

On behalf of defence, witnesses were produced to show that there existed dispute over certain land between the parties and it is alleged that on account of such dispute the accused has been falsely implicated and that no such incident, as is alleged by the prosecutrix, has occurred.

A suggestion has also been given that the simple injuries caused to the victim could be on account of fall from the bicycle and in view of the admitted scenario that no internal injuries was found on the victim, her statement has been disbelieved.
Learned A.G.A. has taken us through the judgment of the court below in order to show inconsistency therein but we find no such inconsistency or perversity in the judgment of the court below.
We have examined the records and we find that the victim herself has disclosed her age to be 22 years.

The age otherwise does not carry much weight in this case, as the trial court on the basis of evidence on record has doubted the case set up by the prosecution with regard to the alleged commissioning of offence of rape for valid reasons.
The delay of two months in disclosing the main offence otherwise remains unexplained.
The dispute between the parties in respect of agricultural land is also not questioned.

In such circumstances, we are of the view that the view taken by the court below is clearly a permissible view, in the facts of the case, and just because a different view could be taken would ordinarily not be a ground for this Court to interfere with the order of acquittal.

In such circumstances, we find that neither any triable issue is raised before us in this appeal nor any State Of U.P. vs Rambaran S/O Bhojraj Yadav on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140814856/
